questions.q1: Finish this sentence without using financial terminology: I want money to eventually give me the ability to…
questions.q2: Rank what matters most to you financially.
questions.q3: What does “financial independence” actually mean to you?
questions.q4: What age would you like work to become optional?
questions.q5: How important is maximizing wealth versus enjoying more money today? Where do you naturally fall on that spectrum?
questions.q6: Think about the last year. What are the five biggest financial decisions you've had to think about?
questions.q7: Which decisions required the most research, spreadsheets, ChatGPT conversations, mental energy, or second-guessing?
questions.q8: What financial questions do you repeatedly revisit because you're never fully satisfied with the answer?
questions.q9: What parts of your finances do you feel extremely confident managing yourself?
questions.q10: What parts do you understand but frankly don't want to spend time managing?
questions.q11: What areas do you suspect you could be doing better in, even if nothing is obviously wrong?
questions.q12: Have you ever thought, “I'm probably leaving money on the table somewhere”? If so, where?
questions.q13: If Penny could continuously evaluate the household, which areas should it understand?
questions.q14: Which question is more valuable to you?
questions.q15: Imagine you have an additional $25,000 available tomorrow. List the possibilities you would personally consider, whether you want Penny to rank them, and what it would need to know before you'd trust that ranking.
questions.q16: Would you want Penny to actively identify idle or suboptimally deployed money without you asking? What would a great recommendation look like?
questions.q17: What investment decisions do you actually want to make personally because you enjoy them?
questions.q18: Which investment decisions would you happily delegate?
questions.q19: Rank how valuable these investment capabilities are.
questions.q21: What major decisions over the next 5–10 years are likely to have meaningful financial consequences? Think beyond purchases: career, family, housing, lifestyle, time off, etc.
questions.q22: For a major decision like a house, what would you actually want Penny to answer?
questions.q23: How valuable would this experience be: “Compare buying a $600k, $750k and $900k house. Optimize the recommendation around the life I told you I want.”
questions.q24: What other decisions would you want to model this way?
questions.q25: Would you want Penny to proactively say, “You can afford this, but I don't think you should do it based on the goals you've told me matter most”? How comfortable are you with Penny challenging your decisions?
questions.q26: Besides financial data, what should Penny understand to give genuinely good advice?
questions.q27: Which of those things should Penny learn once, and which might change enough that Penny should periodically ask again?
questions.q28: Would you want Penny to remember statements like “I'd rather work two extra years than compromise substantially on our house” or “Being able to leave a job I dislike is more important than maximizing lifetime wealth”? Would those preferences make recommendations meaningfully better?
questions.q29: Rank what you'd most want to see first when you open Penny on a random Tuesday morning.
questions.q30: Which feels more valuable: a dashboard you regularly inspect, or an assistant that monitors things and only brings you in when something deserves attention? Why?
questions.q31: How frequently would you genuinely want to interact with Penny if it were working perfectly?
questions.q32: What event should cause Penny to proactively contact you?
questions.q33: What would Penny need to show before you would change your financial behavior based on its recommendation?
questions.q34: How much explanation do you personally want by default?
questions.q35: Which recommendations would you require especially strong evidence for?
questions.q36: Which actions, if any, would you eventually allow Penny to execute after approval?
questions.q37: Are there actions you would never allow software to execute regardless of trust?
questions.q38: Choose the three outcomes you'd pay the most for.
questions.q40: If Penny worked perfectly, what would it do that you cannot easily accomplish today using your current combination of financial apps, spreadsheets, research, ChatGPT, and your own judgment?
questions.q41: What's the first moment during onboarding that would make you think, “Okay, this is actually valuable”?
questions.q42: What's the recurring experience that would make you still pay for Penny two years later?
questions.q43: If Penny saved you meaningful time, improved decisions, and gave you confidence that your entire financial life was optimized appropriately, what would you realistically pay per month? Why?
questions.q44: Final constraint exercise: Penny can only do THREE things exceptionally well in V1. What are they?

answers.q1: Comfortably handle day to day expenses and the occasional splurge for myself, my wife, and kids without needing to work.
answers.q3: It means I can afford anything within reason without needing to work. It means I can comfortably pay expenses for every day living - house, cars, kids, and a few times a year a larger splurge for a family trip, or a larger purchase. It means I my wife and I could live in the house we live in until we're in our 90s. It means we could leave enough to our kids to provide them a meaningful nest egg.
answers.q5: I am 80% maximizing wealth, 20% enjoying today
answers.q6:
1. Needed to see if I should finance a car or take money out of my brokerage to pay for it in cash.
2. Needed to see how long I could last on my expenses if I lost my job - with and without my wife also working
3. Needed to see if it was worth spending $30k to replace my concrete driveway while I was also replacing the roof
4. Needed to see if I should reallocate a good chunk of my brokerage account from the S&P to semiconductor indices
5. Needed to see which subscriptions I have I could stop paying for.
answers.q7: Figuring out how long I could last if I lost my job took by far the most. The finance car vs cash payment was also some decent number crunching. And the subscription finding one took a few hours.
answers.q8:
- How long could I last with my current liquid accounts if I didn't work
- At what age could I be financially independent if neither my wife nor I had a job
- What would the total household income need to be to support our lifestyle without retiring early - and what does that toggle look like between lower income/happier job and early retirement
answers.q9: Pretty much everything minus tax loss harvesting and tax management
answers.q10: I don't want to keep having to number crunch to find the answers to the 3 questions in q8. I want something to do it for me and I can press on the details to simulate what if scenarios when needed without losing my main plan. Having the ability to create multiple plans and keep them up to date at a glance would be incredible.
answers.q11: Largely just automating what's in Q8. And advising me on ways to get tax breaks so I can keep those in mind.
answers.q12: I don't think I'm leaving meaningful money on the table anywhere right now. But that's where I just don't know what I don't know.
answers.q14: B. Given everything happening in my financial life, what should I change?
answers.q14_why: I want to know what moves I can do to improve my situation toward my goals and why
answers.q15: It's not much of a decision - I would put all of that in my brokerage acct and likely invest in the S&P. I have enough savings to where any additional lump sums would all go into my brokerage. Even if I suddenly got $1 million, it would go there too.
answers.q16:
Yes - this seems like an essential feature to me. It would be like "You have $x more sitting in checking beyond your 6 month safety net. If you invest that in your brokerage you could turn that into much more in the next few years"

The future forecasting wording is where we'd need to be careful, but that is the type of insight I would want.
answers.q17: I don't want Penny to tell me what my portfolio I should invest in. I just want it to tell me which accounts to put money in and when depending on how it lines up with my life goals.
answers.q20: C. I think option B is best. Here's why.
answers.q20_why: I don't want it to take the action - at least not yet. Just have it be the expert and tell me what to do and why, and possibly how to do it if I don't really know - since many consumers may not know how to do the action.
answers.q21:
My wife and I will likely have 2-3 kids in that time.
We will also be taking 1-2 trips a year to visit her family in Colombia, which each cost roughly $2500
q22: What lifestyle sacrifices does it create?
What assets should fund the purchase?
answers.q23_why: That is the exact sort of insight that would be very useful - it largely depends on what sort of recommendations it comes back with though
answers.q24:
Car purchases at different price ranges
Other large purchases with optionality (e.g. do I need this new concrete driveway. What do I give up if I take this expensive trip to hawaii, etc)
answers.q25:
Very comfortable as long as it explains why and I can have a conversation about it with Penny. That challenging is the exact thing I want it to do as long as it makes sense. I don't want it to just support bad decisions.

That said it should recommend better options that still allow me to do what I want if they are available.
q26: How much financial uncertainty stresses me
How much I enjoy managing investments
answers.q27: I think it should evaluate all of them every once in a while - things all change over time
answers.q30: An assistant - I already have a ton of dashboards. I want something that's a really simple interface but is really smart.
answers.q32:
- Extra money I could reallocate to my brokerage
- If I'm not allocating enough funds to retirement accounts/HSA given my disposable income
- If my investment or spending decisions are making a noticeable dent in my FI age (either positive or negative). I would want it to both give me kudos, or coach me.
answers.q33: An explanation that makes sense, along with a chat window I can have a conversation about it to understand better. I would want Penny to generate charts and graphics and provide references so I can double check it's work as well if I need to.
answers.q34: Concise by default, full analysis available on demand
answers.q35: I would want progressive disclosure for everything.
answers.q37: Yes - any of them. Both because I don't trust AI enough yet to do it correctly. And there are a lot of compliance concerns with doing that which I don't want Penny to support yet.
q38: Discover opportunities I wouldn't have noticed
answers.q39: A. Build wealth without becoming a financial expert.
answers.q40: There's nothing it could do I can't do on my own. It would just make those things much easier and automated.
answers.q41: Finding either additional savings or cashflow to reallocate to a different account with a reason why. And creating a durable strategy against that going forward
answers.q42: Continuing to make sure I'm optimizing my cashflow and account allocation positions for my goals. It would be my finance goal assistant for FI for years and years to come.
answers.q43: $20 if it really was proving it's worth
answers.q44:
1. Finding either additional savings or cashflow to reallocate to a different account with a reason why
2. Have a chat to dig into why and understand the recommendations better
3. Understand my situation, financial goals and evaluate my portfolio against them to tell me how I'm doing.
